heroHeadline: RSF Drone Kills 14 at Chad-Border Market; Chad Closes Sudan Frontier — Burhan Announces Post-RSF Political Dialogue on Eid
heroSubtitle: On Day 1138, an RSF drone struck the weekly market in Al-Tina, a West Darfur town on the Sudan-Chad border, on May 25, killing at least 14 civilians — mostly women vendors — prompting Chad to condemn the attack, convene an emergency Defence Council, and close its Sudan border, threatening the principal refugee and humanitarian aid corridor into Darfur. In a near-simultaneous strike on May 25, RSF drones targeted RAC leader Musa Hilal's compound in Mustariha, North Darfur, killing several of his commanders while Hilal survived and his son was injured — the second major RSF intra-Rizeigat assassination attempt of the war. On May 26, MSF reported a fast-spreading cholera outbreak in Khartoum: 2,500 cases in three weeks, 633 cases and 24 deaths on May 23 alone, with over 1 million children at risk as the city's destroyed water infrastructure fuels disease spread one year after SAF expelled the RSF from the capital. IOM documented 46,000 newly displaced people in West Kordofan during May alone. On Eid al-Adha (May 27), Gen. Burhan announced plans for a comprehensive political dialogue inside Sudan to formulate a new governance structure, explicitly excluding groups 'whose hands are dripping with the blood of the Sudanese people' — framing a post-RSF political process while both sides continue military operations. SAF drone strikes on RSF positions in North Kordofan on May 27 accompany ongoing multi-front pressure. Total displacement remains 14 million+; 19.5 million face acute food insecurity as the June–August lean-season peak approaches and Chad's border closure threatens Darfur's humanitarian lifeline.
